<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0b49f00d91f84ddf2646255b85c65a26124c78b7` — the merge of head `2f6eef1ff7e0e8914b948b6f8fe1019245f71b81` into base `c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0b49f00d91f84ddf2646255b85c65a26124c78b7 && git checkout 0b49f00d91f84ddf2646255b85c65a26124c78b7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5 2f6eef1ff7e0e8914b948b6f8fe1019245f71b81 && git checkout -B drift-repro c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5 && git merge --no-ff 2f6eef1ff7e0e8914b948b6f8fe1019245f71b81

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head `c87aab92dc10611ce68b48d85d021b5e5182545c` is the dev round's final head (os-dev-report 6923421510 on #33664). The area declares it final for review.

- **Build.** Option A1 under seat route B (6917462284). An engine-internal single-hop relation group key that no wire request carries, so the public `groupBy` is unchanged.
  - Each related read is planned as the caller through the existing related-read plan; there is no second read-scope leaf.
  - driver-sql compiles a LEFT JOIN onto the scoped and tenant-walled parent.
  - service-analytics tries the joined path and falls back to the unchanged FK-expand on a decline or a 4xx.
  - MongoDB and OData keep FK-expand, and the up-front refusal belongs to #33876.
- **Pins.**
  - Parity: 3 callers × 4 shapes, `(restricted)` included.
  - Read scope and tenant wall on the joined parent.
  - The over-bind-limit case: 33,000 FKs answered 500 before and are answered 200 joined.
  - Six ablations, each red, then restored.
- **Bench**, SQLite, admin:
  - 400k lines: 500 before, 200 after (p50 529 ms).
  - 200k lines: p50 220 ms before, 241 ms after. The joined statement costs about 1.5× db time under the bind limit; this is noted in Acceptance notes.
  - PG bench: NOT MEASURED, because the local PG server aborted.
- **Tier.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34430`: not governed, 1635 changed lines (≤ 3000). `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `!`, no narrowing arm. The area lands it.
- **Owed on this head.** L1 (L1-a) and green CI. CI was in progress at this post.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read; landing waits on CI) · Head-sha: c87aab92dc10611ce68b48d85d021b5e5182545c · 2026-11-16T17:16Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-A, reading the final head named in dev report 6923421510 on #33664. I read card #33664, seat route B (record 6917462284), the PR body, and the full diff against merge base `c37e47a5`: 13 files, +1579/−56, seven commits. The area asked me to look hardest at two points: whether the related read is planned as the caller with no second read-scope leaf (ADR-0139 D6), and whether the tenant wall sits on the joined parent. Both hold.

- **Card relation.** `Fixes #33664`, which is right. The divergence from the card's Expected (MongoDB and OData keep the FK-expand instead of a stable 400) follows route B 6917462284, and the PR body says that refusal belongs to #33876.
- **(1) The related read is planned as the caller, with one copy of the leaf (ADR-0139 D6).**
  - `planRelationGroups` builds each relation's related read as the engine's own `aggregate` on the related object. It runs under the caller's merged context, grouped by `['id', ...attrs]` with a `count(id)`, and the strategy's `relatedReadScope` is its `where`. That is the read `resolveFkAttr` ran, minus its id list.
  - That read is stopped at its driver call through the existing `planRelationSemiJoinLeaf` and `RELATION_SCOPE_PLAN` (`scopePlan.capture(ast.where, aggregateOptions)` in `aggregate`, after `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`). So the CRUD gate, every read middleware, row scope, the field-level group-by gate on the attribute, and the stored-field doors all run on it as they do on any read.
  - At the outer read's executor boundary, `relationGroupJoinsAtBoundary` asks the existing `plannedRelationLeafVerdict` with the outer driver options. A `read` verdict or no verdict declines. A deny sentinel hands a `null` parent, and `compose` hands `ReadableIds.compose(leaf, verdict.scope)`.
  - `relation-semi-join.ts` is not touched, so there is no second copy of the read-scope leaf or its verdict. The ablation "compose with `undefined` instead of the planned scope" goes red (1/14).
- **(2) The tenant wall sits on the joined parent.** In `sql-driver-aggregation.ts` the derived table is `getBuilder(related)`. Then `applyTenantScope(sub, related, options)` applies the wall with this read's options, which `plannedRelationLeafVerdict` has proved are the related read's own (ADR-0139 D3). Then `applyFilters(sub, parent.scope, options)` applies the scope. This is the same order and the same two calls as `readableIdsSubquery` (`sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts:136`). The ablation that deletes `applyTenantScope` goes red (3 cases), and the analytics suite pins a cross-tenant FK under `(restricted)` for an admin of org B.
- **The join cannot multiply rows.** The derived table selects the primary key `id` with no grouping, so each child row joins at most one related row and every measure aggregates the rows it did before. The resolved column `CASE WHEN __rgN_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END` is grouped, so a real NULL attribute stays apart from an unresolved row. `relationGroupJoinsOf` refuses, with a 500 before anything compiles, any parent that `isComposedReadableIds` does not recognize.
- **Decline, never half-served.**
  - Registry declines, before anything is read: a driver outside `RELATION_GROUP_JOIN_COMPILING_DRIVERS`, a federated object, a multi-valued relation, an object mismatch, and a related object `relationSemiJoinServes` keeps the id read for.
  - Late declines: a related read that is not one planned statement, an outer read whose driver options differ, and an aggregate the driver does not answer natively.
  - An outer read middleware that answers without the driver leaves `outcome` unset, and the plugin reads that as `joined: false`.
  - In `ObjectQLStrategy`, any 4xx on the joined path falls back to the unchanged FK-expand, which re-derives the refusal in today's order and envelope. That is pinned by `objectql-echo-non-date-bucket` through an ablation. A 5xx surfaces.
- **Field-level read of the FK itself.** I checked that the joined path does not skip the FK field's own read verdict. The analytics door `assertFieldsReadable` → `namedQueryFields` → `fieldsOfColumnSql` names every hop's relationship field on the object before it (#20986), before any strategy runs. A hidden `bench_line_item.opportunity` is refused there, on both paths. See S1 for the engine-side half.
- **Not a wire key.** `RELATION_GROUP_BY` and `RELATION_GROUP_JOINS` are `Symbol.for` keys, set only by the plugin bridge (read option) and the engine (on the composed AST, after middleware). A dotted public `groupBy` is still refused.
- **Pins.** Read in full:
  - `relation-group-join.test.ts` (14);
  - `sql-driver-relation-group-join.test.ts`, the dialect matrix, at most 3 bindings;
  - `cross-object-relation-group-join.test.ts` (18): parity against the FK-expand for 3 callers × 4 shapes, the explicit buckets, and 33,000 FKs that answer 11,000 per stage where the FK-expand answers 500;
  - two `exempt` rows in `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`.

  The six ablations in the body each went red and were restored.
- **Changeset.** I checked each sentence against the diff: `patch` on all three packages, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, "its CRUD gate, read middlewares, row scope and field-level gate all apply", "the tenant wall bounds the joined table", "Every bucket and measure is the one the old path answered", and "the public `groupBy` still refuses a dotted path". Every one matches the code above.
- **L2.** None is owed. None of the four contract faces is touched (`contract-review.md`): no `packages/spec/src/**` file, `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing declaration, and no governed path. The new `AnalyticsServiceConfig.executeRelationGroupAggregate` is an optional member of a service package's config type, not a published schema. ③'s standing check runs in the right direction: this PR removes an id materialization (`id IN (…)`) and pushes the join down to SQL. So the area's reading of "no" is right, and this ACCEPT is the review of record.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs at 17:15Z): 49 names, 21 success, 16 skipped, 12 still running (Test Core 1–8/8, Build Core, three Type Check jobs), and 0 failed. Landing needs all of them green.
- **Base.** PRBASE is the Test Core plan's diff base, and K = 2. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean.

### Should (small; before landing, or a named card)

- **S1. The engine's own field gate no longer sees the FK on the joined path.**
  - On the FK-expand path the base aggregate groups by `opportunity`, so plugin-security's aggregate input gate (step 2.5b, `ast.groupBy`) judges that field a second time. On the joined path `replaced` removes it from `groupBy`, and the join rides a symbol the middleware never sees. The analytics door still refuses it first (above), so nothing leaks in the shipped composition, but the engine's belt for that field is gone on this path.
  - The docblock's "Holding the key grants nothing" is therefore slightly too strong: the key does let a caller skip the engine's field verdict on the base relation field.
  - Either have the engine judge each `relation.field` with the same field gate, or reword that sentence to say the base relation field's field-level read is the caller's to judge (as the analytics door does, #20986).
  - Either way, add one case to `cross-object-relation-group-join.test.ts`: a caller whose field permissions hide `bench_line_item.opportunity` gets the same 403 with the hook wired as without it.

### Notes (not blocking)

- **N1.** Under the bind limit, the joined path is slower on SQLite: about 1.5× database time and about 1.1× request p50 at 20k parents, measured on a shared box. PostgreSQL was not measured. Every SQL deployment takes the joined path first. That is a fair trade for a p1 that fixes a 500, but it is worth a line on the card so a later bench reads it as known.
- **N2.** The derived table restates `readableIdsSubquery`'s two calls (wall, then scope) rather than calling it. That is three lines and in the same order today, but it is a second place to keep in step. `readableIdsSubquery(join.parent, options).clearSelect().select(…)` would keep one.
- **N3.** The body's out-of-scope note (an unset FK buckets under `(restricted)`, a label that reads as a permission outcome) is pre-existing, and parity is kept on purpose. It needs a card if nobody has filed one.

Landing: not Tier H, and no L2 owed. Area o1-A lands it once every check is green and S1 has landed or been carded.

Final head · PR #34430 · Fixes #33664 · area o1-A · head 2f6eef1f · 2026-11-16T18:57Z

Head `2f6eef1ff7e0e8914b948b6f8fe1019245f71b81` supersedes `c87aab92` (6923496210) with three commits from round r2 (dev report 6925969078 on #33664). The area declares it final. The body was rewritten at this head (body-only).

- **L1 S1 (6923610947): fixed in the engine, with no second copy of any gate.** On the joined path, the middleware chain now sees the base aggregate grouped by each relation field that `groupBy` does not already name. Only the statement handed to the driver drops those keys, and the join takes their place there. So the field gate and every other group-key guard judge the lookup field exactly as they do on the FK-expand's base read.
  - Pinned at the analytics door, engine-level (the relation group key handed directly, for a caller who may not read the field: 403), and on the objectql chain.
  - Ablation: removing the judged keys turns the engine-level pin and the chain pin red; restored, both green.
- **CI red on `c87aab92`: answered by classification.** The red was the second-object read-exposure pin (#22661).
  - The joined path's target exposure is decided at the analytics door: `assertObjectsExposed` runs over every hop's object before any strategy, so both paths share one verdict.
  - `relation-group-join.ts` is classified `decided` on that door, as `relation-filter-lowering.ts` is. The pin gains the `aggregate` operation and the door function in its exact roster; its scan and checks are unchanged.
  - Behaviour pins: an object with API access disabled answers 404 and a method not allowed answers 405, on both paths. Ablation of the door turns both red.
- **Not taken:** L1 N2. It needs an edit in `sql-driver.ts`, outside the same-file bound. N1 and N3 were left as notes.
- **Readings.**
  - Suites: objectql 13485, driver-sql 4331 (247 skipped) and service-analytics 5318 (335 skipped) passed. Typechecks: exit 0.
  - Gates: 82 derived, 82 run, all exit 0.
  - CI on this head: 55 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Tier.** Not governed, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Owed: the L1 delta (L1-a, on 6923610947). Then the area lands it.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, delta) · Head-sha: 2f6eef1ff7e0e8914b948b6f8fe1019245f71b81 · 2026-11-16T18:59Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-A, reading the delta from my ACCEPT 6923610947 at `c87aab92` to the final head named in dev report 6925969078. The delta is three commits with no merge: 6 files, +273/−10.

- **S1 (closed, in the engine — the stronger of the two routes offered).**
  - *What changed.* `aggregate` now builds the middleware chain's AST with each relation field the join replaces appended to `groupBy`, unless `groupBy` already names it (`relationFieldsJudgedAsGroupKeys`; structured `{ field }` items count as named).
  - *What the chain sees.* Every middleware, plugin-security's aggregate input gate (step 2.5b) among them, judges `opportunity` exactly as on the FK-expand's base read.
  - *Where the field leaves.* Only after the chain, at the driver call, does `withoutJudgedRelationFields` remove those added string keys. The join takes their place, and an absent own `groupBy` stays absent.
  - *What is untouched.* The static doors before the chain still judge the caller's own `query.groupBy`, and `assertRelationGroupRequestShape` still reads that same list, so the output-column checks are unchanged.
  - *Docs.* The docblock now says the engine "judges the base read as grouped by each relation field". The new changeset sentence ("a caller who may not read that field is refused exactly as before") matches the code.
- **S1 pins.**
  - `relation-group-join.test.ts`: the chain sees `groupBy` with the field, and the driver's statement does not.
  - `cross-object-relation-group-join.test.ts`, through the analytics door: the same 403 with the join wired as without it, and no relation group request handed to the engine.
  - The same file, at the engine, past the door: the request is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` for that caller with `outcome` unset, the same envelope as the FK-expand.
  - The same file, a control: a caller who may read the field is joined, and no row carries `opportunity`.
- **The #22661 classification and the core pin edit.** The red on `c87aab92` was right: `relation-group-join.ts` calls `referenceTargetOf`, so the enumeration requires a row for it. The row is sound.
  - *`kind: 'decided'`.* The related object is reached only through the analytics door. The pin's own header already records that this door "judges every hop's object for `aggregate` over `queryObjects`". `assertObjectsExposed` (`api-exposure-door.ts:274`) calls `apiExposureDenialReason(enable, ANALYTICS_OPERATION)`, and `callCtx` runs it over the full `queryObjects` set, hops included, before the read admission. That happens ahead of any strategy, so ahead of the join.
  - *Operation `aggregate`.* That is what the door asks, and what the FK-expand's related read was. Widening the `operation` union to take it is the minimum edit.
  - *The exact roster.* The `decision.fn` roster gains `assertObjectsExposed`, the one new decided row. Nothing else in the pin moved, and no existing row was relaxed.
  - *The behaviour pin it names.* The new `[#22661]` describe asserts, per refused declaration, the same 404/405 envelope on both paths, with no relation group request reaching the engine, plus a served control.
  - *Precedent.* This follows the `relation-filter-lowering.ts` row: an engine module whose second-object read is decided by the door that hands it the request.
  - *What it relies on.* The row stands because the analytics strategy is `RELATION_GROUP_BY`'s only caller. Any second caller of that option would have to ask the related object's exposure itself, and the row's `wiring` and `pin` name only the analytics door. See N1.
- **L2 reading: unchanged, none owed.** None of the four contract faces is touched. The pin edit is a test file in `packages/core/src/security`, not a published schema, a governed path, `Clause-②` or a narrowing. It adds a row and widens a test-local union, which tightens the enumeration rather than relaxing it. The seat may still want it named in the hand-off as security-adjacent, since it edits a security pin's roster.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 70 names, 56 success, 13 skipped, and the last running job finished green while I read. 0 failed.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `c9ef6538` (Test Core plan), and K = 6. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean.

### Note (not blocking)

- **N1.** Give `RELATION_GROUP_BY`'s docblock one sentence saying that its caller answers the related object's API exposure (#22661, today the analytics door's `assertObjectsExposed`), next to "Holding the key grants nothing". The engine does not ask it, and the pin row holds only as long as the analytics door is the one caller. That can ride any later edit of the file.

Landing: not Tier H, and no L2 owed. Area o1-A lands it.
